question:
A 22-year-old female presents to a psychiatric clinic reporting persistent sadness and fatigue following
her husband's departure two months ago. Her symptoms have worsened over the past three weeks,
characterized by: - Late-night crying episodes affecting sleep - Difficulty concentrating at work with
increased errors - Extended weekend sleep (10-12 hours) with low motivation - Sensation of heaviness
in legs, described as "anchors pulling down" - Maintained social engagement and participation in
events despite symptoms Based on this clinical presentation, which medication would be the most
appropriate initial prescription? Answer Choices: (A) Venlafaxine (B) Paroxetine (C) Bupropion (D)

Sertraline (E) Duloxetine (F) Phenelzine (G) Mirtazapine (H) Fluoxetine (I) Escitalopram (J)
Amitriptyline
 A. Escitalopram
B. Phenelzine
C. Sertraline
D. Fluoxetine
E. Paroxetine
F. Bupropion
G. Amitriptyline
H. Venlafaxine
I. Duloxetine
J. Mirtazapine
